text: The box shall play a household member's recording of a book when a card is put on it, and shall keep every recording the household has ever played.
rationale: The design record names the recordings as the only irreplaceable thing in the project. A player that is cheap to rebuild and expensive to lose from has to be built around that asymmetry.

text: The box shall be the keeper of the household's recordings: no request arriving over the network shall destroy a recording a card has ever played.
rationale: As written, the box API has no authorisation, PUT /api/card overwrites a binding with no history, orphanTitles() labels the old recording dead weight, and DELETE /api/title removes it. Any phone on the box's access point can do this in two requests (proposals/morphyx-keeper.mjs, part 1).

text: Binding a card shall append to the card's history and shall never erase what the card played before.
acceptance: T-KEEP-HISTORY passes: after any sequence of PUT /api/card requests, every title a card has ever been bound to is listed in its history in order, and re-binding to an earlier title restores it.
rationale: Re-pointing a card is the design's best feature (D1). It should cost a line in a ledger, not a recording.

text: A title that any card has ever been bound to shall not be removed by a network request alone.
acceptance: T-KEEP-WIRE passes: on 200 random sequences of add, bind, enrol and delete requests (seeds 1-200), every once-bound title remains present or archived; and the negative control (bindCard and DELETE as written) is caught on at least one seed.
rationale: Measured in proposals/morphyx-keeper.mjs: keeper 200/200, control caught 200/200. The phone is a messenger, not an owner.

text: Removing a once-bound title shall require the box's back button to be held during the request, and shall move the files to an archive folder on the SD card rather than erase them.
acceptance: T-KEEP-HANDS passes: DELETE without the held button is refused and logged with the rule that refused it; with the button held, the title leaves the manifest and its files are found under the archive path with sizes unchanged.
rationale: Authority goes to whoever is physically at the box, the same principle as the volume end stop. A 32 GiB SD holds about 3119 h of speech at 64 kbps, so archiving rather than erasing costs nothing the household would miss.

text: While enrolment is armed, a tag that already carries a tape card id shall not be written or re-bound.
acceptance: T-KEEP-ENROL passes: a bound card placed during the 60 s window is refused (or played, never written), the window stays armed, and a blank tag placed afterwards is written and bound.
rationale: protocol.js says the next tag on the pad is written; firmware/ says the next blank tag. The two documents disagree, and the child holding the deck decides which card lands first. The firmware page's word should be the rule.

text: The box shall export its whole library (manifest, history and audio) as one file that a fresh box can import to play every card the same way.
acceptance: T-KEEP-BACKUP passes: export, import into an empty simulated box, and every card id resolves to the same track list and resume setting.
rationale: SD cards fail and toddlers post them through floorboards. The phone's own voice memos are a backup of the audio but not of which card plays what.

text: Where a child's safety or a card's placement is decided, a printed shape shall decide it, not a setting.
rationale: The design already chose a potentiometer end stop over a software limit and a nest over the child being careful. These leaves keep later simplifications from undoing that.

text: The nest shall seat a 63 x 88 mm card over the antenna by geometry alone, in either orientation, with no metal between card and antenna.
acceptance: I-HANDS-NEST: the parametric enclosure model computes 0.5 to 1.5 mm clearance per side, and a printed nest accepts 20 drops of a card from 10 cm by a child without the card resting outside it.
rationale: Same constraint as tape/hardware's list. The drop count is the test a CAD model cannot run.

text: The maximum volume shall be limited by a fixed resistance or a printed rotation stop that cannot be changed without tools, not by firmware.
acceptance: I-HANDS-STOP: the schematic shows the limit in hardware, the firmware has no volume ceiling that the hardware does not also enforce, and the knob cannot reach past the stop by hand.
rationale: A firmware ceiling is a setting someone can change over the same open API. The measured dB(A) figure belongs to Modulo's TAPE-SAFE-VOL; this leaf fixes where the limit lives.

text: The box shall be buildable by the household from printed parts and the parts.json bill of materials, with the enclosure generated from the same data the firmware uses.
rationale: The lab's test: an object gets built when the household agrees it is worth having. The build itself is the household activity, so it has to be possible without one person who understands everything.

text: Enclosure dimensions that depend on parts (card size, speaker diameter, cell length, board outline) shall be read from parts.json or lib/, not typed into the model.
acceptance: T-MAKE-PARAM passes: changing the speaker diameter in a copy of parts.json changes the grille and baffle in the generated model, and a lint finds no literal millimetre value that duplicates a parts.json field.
rationale: Pin map as code and parts as data are already the house standard (tape/system). The enclosure is the one artefact that would otherwise break it.

text: Each of the eight build stages shall end at a gate that someone other than its builder can check with the tools marked owned in parts.json.
acceptance: I-MAKE-STAGES: every stage on tape/build names its gate, the owned tool that checks it, and who checked it on the household's build.
rationale: A build that only its designer can verify is one person's project that the others watch.

text: A household member's recording shall play from a card on the printed box, on the household's own shelf.
acceptance: D-HOUSE: one book recorded on a phone, bound to a card, and played through to FINISHED on the built box by someone who did not build it.
rationale: Shared word for word with Modulo's tree. Nothing else earns the tree its value.

text: After a card is re-pointed to a second reader's recording, the first reader's recording shall still be playable by re-binding.
acceptance: D-HOUSE-REPOINT: on the built box, two household members read the same book; the card is moved to the second recording, then back, and the first plays from where it was left.
rationale: The household will re-point cards. The day it does is the day this arrangement is tested for real.

text: The box shall keep a copy of its card bindings in its own flash, rewritten on every bind and whenever it accepts a bindings file at boot, shall restore the bindings from that copy and log the restore when no bindings file (cards.json, or failing that cards.new) parses at boot, and shall treat a bindings file that parses as authoritative.
acceptance: T-KEEP-ABSENT passes: in the des box model, an SD returned with cards.json missing or torn leaves 0 of 200 decks scrambled; the as-written mutant (missing file means no bindings) and the present-means-decides mutant (torn file means no bindings) each scramble at least 1 of 200 (proposals/modulo-torn.mjs). A cards.json that parses and contains {} clears the bindings and is not overridden. A hand-edited cards.json followed by a missing file before any bind restores the edited deck, not the pre-edit one: 0 of 200 (proposals/morphyx-adopt.mjs, undo row; mirror-on-bind-only scrambles 200 of 200).Restored bindings that name folders missing from the SD are dropped and logged.
rationale: In TAPE1 the SD is the only home of which card plays which book, and it goes through a laptop every fortnight. If cards.json comes back missing, every card reads as fresh and binds in whatever order the child puts the deck down: 200/200 households with 8 books scrambled, a mean of 7.1 of 8 cards on the wrong book (proposals/morphyx-absence.mjs). No audio is lost, but the binding is. The rule is that a missing or torn file is not a decision: only a file someone wrote changes the deck. In the merged tree this sits under TAPE1-STORE.
